questions.key_step: Non-trivial solution means D=0; column operations then reduce it to 1/(1+a)+... = 2.
questions.justification: Routine chain: write homogeneous system, set D=0, one column operation, algebra. No insight beyond the standard criterion.

questions.key_step: Rewrite the three definitions as a homogeneous system and set its determinant to zero.
questions.justification: Same device as Q1 with a small expansion; routine but the system must be set up from the definitions.

questions.key_step: Spot that cos q·(1) − sin q·(2) reproduces the left side of (3), then solve a rotation system.
questions.justification: Elimination with trig identities and a rotation-type 2x2 solve; stages are easy but the combination must be seen. Needs an unstated cos q ≠ sin q + 1 condition.

questions.key_step: Subtract equations to get (λ−3)z = μ−10 and classify.
questions.justification: Standard unique/infinite/none analysis of a 3x3 parametric system: two subtractions and three cases, no new idea.
questions.nearest_anchor: 2023-P1-Q14 (L3, easier: only one parameter pair, no matching)

questions.key_step: Compute D, D1, D2, D3 for a parametric 3x3 system and treat K=2 separately.
questions.justification: Four 3x3 determinants with a parameter: routine concept but heavy, error-prone computation and a separate degenerate case.

questions.key_step: Cramer's rule gives x=(d-2b)/(ad-bc); then minimise over distinct digits.
questions.justification: Short route once x is written, but the optimisation needs casework with signs and distinctness where one slip changes the answer; no options to check.

questions.key_step: D = 7(λ+5); at λ=−5 solve with a parameter and verify the third equation.
questions.justification: Standard parametric 3x3 system: one determinant, one parametric solve and a check; no insight needed.

questions.key_step: Recognise Vandermonde-type determinants (or the cubic with roots a, b, c) so everything cancels.
questions.justification: Cramer's rule with three structured determinants; the factorisation pattern must be recognised, alternate (Vieta) is one line.

questions.key_step: Scale columns by a,b,c to expose squares, then add all columns so s factors out.
questions.justification: Determinant manipulation with a non-obvious scaling trick and heavy symbolic bookkeeping; the structure (rank-one + scalar) is not immediately visible.

questions.key_step: Column differences create (0,0,1) and turn tan differences into cot differences; recognise a product of three differences.
questions.justification: Chain of operations with half-angle trig and a hidden Vandermonde-type factorisation; idea is moderately non-obvious, algebra manageable.

questions.key_step: Multiply Δ by the row-scaled determinant to get a determinant with d on the diagonal and f elsewhere.
questions.justification: Product-of-determinants (Gram) trick is a known but not routine idea; then a standard C1→C1+C2+C3 evaluation.

questions.key_step: Expand all three expressions and compare, or use the structure u = xP + yQ.
questions.justification: Three long polynomial expansions with many terms; no single trick is required but a slip in the 2xy terms ruins it.

questions.key_step: Compute D and the Di and treat λ=5 separately (with a consistency check).
questions.justification: Standard parametric system; routine though determinant-heavy.

questions.key_step: Notice A is Hermitian: conj(A)=Aᵀ, so det is its own conjugate.
questions.justification: One recognition step (Hermitian) and two standard determinant properties; no computation.

questions.key_step: Use column operations with C3 to produce the factor (1+a²+b²) twice.
questions.justification: Short column-operation chain with a visible target; slightly longer algebra.

questions.key_step: Recognise that every permutation product has argument sum 0 so product = sum, then cancel.
questions.justification: Non-routine proof: needs the tan identity, the observation about every product, and a cancellation argument; idea availability is low and execution is delicate.

questions.key_step: Factor Δ as V·[xyz·e2 − e1] (generalised Vandermonde), then use the G.P. form.
questions.justification: Needs the factorisation of a non-standard determinant (idea availability moderate) and a short G.P. substitution; the options help.

questions.key_step: Vieta sum and product give equality in AM–GM, so the roots coincide and Δ has equal rows.
questions.justification: One neat idea (AM–GM equality) and a final observation; the options guide the student.

questions.key_step: Reuse the factorisation of Δ; in an A.P. the vanishing factor reduces to xz(2y²+xz)=3.
questions.justification: Uses the factorisation from the earlier question and one clean substitution; options guide the student but distinctness must be noticed.

questions.key_step: Compute D and Di; D3 = a−2 pins the infinite case at a = 2.
questions.justification: Routine parametric-system analysis with three determinants; the options make it easy to eliminate.

questions.key_step: D=0 with a non-zero numerator determinant; the pair (a≠2, b=3).
questions.justification: Same system as the previous question; one more case-split.

questions.key_step: Unique solution iff D≠0.
questions.justification: Direct reading of D = (a−2)(b−3); no decision beyond Q20's setup.

questions.key_step: Entries are defined everywhere so the domain is R; the determinant itself is not needed.
questions.justification: Domain of a trig-polynomial determinant: immediate; closed form is only a check.

questions.key_step: Reduce the determinant to 150 + 100 sin 2x by row operations.
questions.justification: Two row operations and a standard range of a sine; very direct.
